source.evidence: present in AERONET's live 'Active Site Lists (V3) -> Text Format', retrieved from official NASA AERONET homepage on 2026-11-19
source.official_method_limitation: Solar AOD is daylight-derived, not an actual human star detection; V3 lunar AOD may be available only at suitable lunar phases and is a distinct dataset.
source.identification_limit: The list establishes active-site listing, not current measurement availability or that any individual date has quality-assured rows.

retrieval_attempt.explanation: The official data-service URL could not be opened in the available web reader. A separate high-level file download refused because the URL had not been registered as viewed. No measured rows or values were obtained; no retry or proxy used.
retrieval_attempt.no_data_inference: Do not interpret retrieval failure as no AOD existing.

prospective_handoff: Authorized outreach owner/Coordinator: retain unsent RASC email draft pending review; do not infer any volunteer enrollment, site permission or consent.
Before any prospective event, privately obtain exact field site and measure its distance/elevation mismatch versus Halifax AERONET; source must not be treated as colocated by city name alone.

From the NASA V3 endpoint obtain original timestamped instantaneous Level 2.0 AOD (preferably 550 nm or spectrally verified conversion), raw filename/URL and SHA256 plus QA flags. Never use daily climatology as exact night state.

For actual observing night, register nearby ground station, cloud/adaptation logs, naked-eye negative-to-positive checks and separate directional skyglow; verify atmospheric time gap and local representativeness before admission.

Freeze observer-independent predictor SHA, config, catalogue, atmospheric input selection rule, event selection and uncertainty/error/acceptance limits before accessing outcomes; no Taylor/Jerusalem or protected holdout.
If no valid contemporaneous Level 2.0 exists, label atmospheric AOD UNKNOWN and either apply a predeclared uncertainty/fail-closed rule or exclude from quantitative accurate-time validation.
privacy: No private observer or coordinates; this is a public NASA site locator.
